parts.note: co- as a prefix means a fellow or partner, as in co-worker
a ward is a child in someone's guardianship, often an orphan

explanation.surface: A boy raised alongside another orphan grows up to write plays.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward was an English playwright; the hyphen in 'Fellow-orphan' hides the split into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward was a celebrated English dramatist, author of Private Lives.

clue.text: Freeholder has nowhere to move when he leaves

indicators.note: to move tells us the letters of the word nowhere are shifted around, once he is gone

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A property holder finds himself with no place to go after leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when he leaves' takes H and E out of NOWHERE, leaving NOWRE, which 'to move' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeholder holds land outright, so is its proprietor.

clue.text: Is it suitable to house painters?

definitions.text: Is it suitable to house painters?

indicators.note: to house means one piece is lodged inside the other word

parts.note: apt means suitable or fitting
art men, men of art, are painters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a dwelling would suit a group of artists.
explanation.walkthrough: APT is opened up by ARTMEN; the whole clue also hints at a flat where people live.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a home that would house anyone, painters included.

indicators.note: we're told signals that a word heard spoken is wanted, not one written

parts.note: dolour is a literary word for grief or sorrow

explanation.surface: Wealth is said to bring grief.
explanation.definitionFit: The dollar is a unit of currency, so stands for cash.

parts.note: someone green looks ill or nauseous
tea is a common drink

explanation.surface: A pale, unhealthy-looking person sips a beverage made from raw leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Green tea is made from tea leaves that are dried without being fermented, unlike black tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea consists of tea leaves that have not been oxidised or fermented.

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a board game
silent means without saying anything

explanation.surface: Someone falls quiet yet still gets the message across.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is obvious needs no stating because everyone grasps it already.

parts.note: to be reconciled is to put an end to the quarrel
the anger is what is ended when people make up

explanation.surface: A person accepts the hazard they face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be reconciled' read as a phrase gives two words together: to end anger.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil something is to put it at risk, a verb sense.

clue.text: Censured by Speaker for raising question endlessly

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means the letters read upwards, so backwards
endlessly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to demand is to question or ask firmly

explanation.surface: An MP is reprimanded by the Commons Speaker for pressing a query.
explanation.walkthrough: DEMAND loses its last letter to give DEMAN, and 'raising' turns that round. In the House of Commons the Speaker 'names' an unruly MP, a formal censure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Speaker of the Commons punishes an MP by publicly identifying them, a parliamentary disciplinary sense.

indicators.note: unreliable suggests the letters of sea proved cannot be trusted to stay put

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The ocean turned out treacherous for a sailor trying to get a tap working.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen in secretly is what tapping a telephone line does.

indicators.note: stupidly signals the letters of the word Hun are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
allowed means given permission

explanation.surface: A barbarian warrior was foolishly given leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' rearranges HUN into UNH, followed by ALLOWED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unholy or sinful is wicked, not sanctified.

definitions.meaning: to prompt someone to act is to stir or impel them
to put forward a motion at a meeting

explanation.definitionFit: To stir someone into action, and to put forward a formal motion in debate.

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a tract is a short published pamphlet

explanation.surface: A text is shortened before printing.
explanation.walkthrough: In surveying, to protract is to lay down a plan to scale, hence 'scale down'; the surface suggests reducing size.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveyors plot lines on paper to scale using a protractor, a drafting sense.

parts.note: duds is slang for clothes, so this is someone who refuses to wear any, not someone intolerant of failures

explanation.walkthrough: 'Duds' looks like failures or useless things; it is informal for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes unclothed and so rejects garments altogether.

indicators.note: about means one word goes round another

parts.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard

explanation.surface: A book concerning an elderly lady's house.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme tells of an old woman who lived in a shoe, so footwear is her home.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme, a woman with many children lived inside footwear.

clue.text: Sort of progression on a musical instrument

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: a harmonic progression is a mathematical sequence

explanation.surface: A kind of chord sequence played on an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The mouth organ is a small wind instrument.

clue.text: Live coals start to blaze away

definitions.meaning: a fire burning in an open hearth
to begin shooting, as soldiers do

explanation.definitionFit: A hearth fire of burning coals, and the order to begin shooting at an enemy.

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means this piece comes beneath the other

parts.note: force means compulsion
meat is food

explanation.surface: Someone is force-fed while stuffed full.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcemeat is a seasoned mixture of chopped meat used as a filling for poultry.

clue.text: Unleavened bread — man is working on getting it to rise

parts.note: a chap is a man
to be at something is to be working on it

indicators.note: in a down clue, to rise means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A baker is busy getting the dough up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' turns IT into TI. The surface joke is that this bread never rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapatti is a flat Indian bread made without yeast.

clue.text: Councillor returns thanks to child — Tiny Tim

indicators.note: returns means the word goes backwards

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
a chit is a young child, often a pert girl

explanation.surface: A local councillor sends thanks to a small boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns TA into AT. Tiny Tim is the crippled child in Dickens's A Christmas Carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny Tim is the youngest son of Bob in Dickens's A Christmas Carol, bearing that surname.

clue.text: Stay, but it's correct for outside pair to leave

indicators.note: the first and last letters are removed from the word for correct

parts.note: proper means correct

explanation.surface: Someone is told to remain, since it is right for the outer couple to go.
explanation.walkthrough: PROPER loses its first and last letters. A stay is a rope bracing a ship's mast.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, a stay is a heavy line supporting the mast, a nautical sense.

clue.text: He captured horses with stunted tails, say

indicators.note: say indicates a word heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: stubs are short, stunted ends

explanation.surface: A rider caught horses whose tails had been cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: George Stubbs was an 18th-century English painter famous for his horses; 'captured' means on canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stubbs, the English painter, portrayed horses on canvas.

definitions.meaning: to hold something up is to display it

explanation.definitionFit: A traffic hold-up is a stoppage, and raising an item for others to see displays it.

definitions.meaning: a heap of snow blown by the wind

explanation.definitionFit: To meander aimlessly, and a heap of windblown flakes piled up.

clue.text: Head so burdened, with many points?

definitions.text: Head so burdened, with many points?

parts.words: Head so burdened, with many points?
parts.note: a head weighed down with something pointed suggests a stag carrying its branching horns

explanation.walkthrough: The 'points' are the tines on a stag's horns.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag with large horns has many tines, or points.

clue.text: Exclusive part of Babel — it escaped

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something exclusive slipped out of the Tower of Babel.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclusive group is a select one, the best few.

parts.note: mid means middle or centre

explanation.surface: A skirt sold in the middle of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue reads 'Skin'; the printed page has 'Skirt'.
explanation.definitionFit: A midi is a skirt reaching mid-calf.

clue.text: I am taken in by deceitful blighter's trick

indicators.note: taken in by means the first words are placed inside the jumble
deceitful suggests the letters of blighter's are misleadingly rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter
I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: Someone is fooled by a dishonest rogue's ruse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deceitful' marks the anagram and 'taken in by' the insertion; 'blighter' looks like a person in the surface but only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Thimblerig is the shell game, a swindle with three cups and a pea.

clue.text: Distant object shows the least change

parts.note: far means distant
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: A remote object shows almost no alteration.
explanation.walkthrough: A farthing was the old British quarter-penny coin, the smallest coin.
explanation.definitionFit: This quarter-penny was the lowest-value British coin, so the smallest bit of loose cash.

clue.text: Camp-follower is more refined in speech

indicators.note: in speech signals a word as it is heard spoken

parts.note: subtler means more refined or delicate

explanation.surface: A hanger-on in an army camp speaks with greater refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: A sutler sold provisions to soldiers in camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A sutler was a merchant trailing an army to sell supplies to troops.
